name: State Sponsorship and Commodity Trading Funding of Terrorism
description: Terrorist organisations may receive support from state actors or raise revenue by controlling and trading commodities such as oil, minerals, antiquities and agricultural goods. Trade finance, front companies and commodity brokers can be used to convert resources into funds and move them to the group.

sources.text: FATF, Financing of the Terrorist Organisation Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) (2015)
FATF, Financing of Recruitment for Terrorist Purposes (2018)
FATF, Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment Guidance (2019)

exposure.rationale: Commodity trades (oil, minerals, antiquities) via brokers and front companies; state or quasi-state transfers to non-state actors; barter and cash settlement.

indicators.name: Commodity trade originating from areas controlled by armed groups
indicators.canon: Armed-group territory or sanctioned parties in conflict areas
indicators.desc: Trade, production or payments involve territories controlled by armed groups or parties linked to them.
indicators.ctx: Shipments of oil, minerals, scrap or agricultural goods with origin documentation tied to territory where terrorist groups operate.
indicators.fp: Legitimate producers in border regions can have mixed supply chains.

indicators.name: Trading company with no operational history receives or sends commodity payments
indicators.canon: Newly established customer with rapid high-value activity
indicators.desc: A recently formed customer with little history or track record quickly records large turnover or trades in high-value or restricted goods.
indicators.ctx: Newly formed broker handles large commodity payments, has little physical presence and uses third-country accounts.

indicators.name: Payments to intermediaries in neighbouring transit jurisdictions
indicators.canon: Payments to intermediaries in neighbouring transit jurisdictions
indicators.desc: Commodity proceeds are settled through agents or companies in jurisdictions adjacent to conflict areas and then forwarded onward.
indicators.ctx: Commodity proceeds are settled through agents or companies in jurisdictions adjacent to conflict areas and then forwarded onward.
indicators.fp: Regional hubs are common commercial centres.

indicators.name: Cultural property or antiquities sales with weak provenance
indicators.canon: Cultural property or antiquities sales with weak provenance
indicators.desc: Trade in antiquities or artefacts with gaps in provenance linked to conflict-zone origin.
indicators.ctx: Trade in antiquities or artefacts with gaps in provenance linked to conflict-zone origin.
indicators.fp: Older collections may have incomplete but benign provenance.

indicators.name: Transactions involving entities tied to state support for designated groups
indicators.canon: Transactions involving entities tied to state support for designated groups
indicators.desc: Counterparties publicly linked, by credible reports, to government support for terrorist organisations.
indicators.ctx: Counterparties publicly linked, by credible reports, to government support for terrorist organisations.
indicators.fp: Government-owned entities are widely used in legitimate trade.

indicators.name: Discrepancies between invoice, shipment and payment details
indicators.canon: Trade documents inconsistent with each other
indicators.desc: Bill of lading, invoice, customs, letter of credit or payment details disagree on goods, quantity, price, origin, parties or route.
indicators.ctx: Quantity, price, consignee or route differs across documents in commodity transactions.
indicators.fp: Errors and commercial renegotiation are routine.

indicators.name: Unusual use of cash or barter in commodity deals
indicators.canon: Unusual use of cash or barter in commodity deals
indicators.desc: Settlement via cash, barter or netting arrangements without documentation.
indicators.ctx: Settlement via cash, barter or netting arrangements without documentation.
indicators.fp: Barter and cash remain used in some commodity markets.

indicators.name: Funding flows following government transfers to non-state entities
indicators.canon: Funding flows following government transfers to non-state entities
indicators.desc: Payments from state or quasi-state entities to private firms or individuals lacking evident services.
indicators.ctx: Payments from state or quasi-state entities to private firms or individuals lacking evident services.
indicators.fp: Grants and subsidies to private recipients are common.
